title: When the Spire Wakes
premise: When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, Ada Nakamura discovers her bone-carved charms were never trinkets — they are keys, and she is the last living warden of a country that has been quietly erased from the world's memory. Hunted by the Ministry of Unmaking and guided by the voices of the dead who remember what no one else can, Ada gathers a ragged found family: a disgraced ward-singer, a dragon-fire keeper's orphaned apprentice, and a smuggler who once sold her out. To restore the stars and reopen the door out of the vanished country, Ada must carve her own name into the Spire's heart — accepting that doing so will erase every memory anyone holds of her. In the end she chooses belonging over identity: the Spire wakes, the country returns, and her family carries her memory for her, rebuilding it story by story until she can step back through the door as someone new.
about_author: U. M. Ashgrove is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring carved ivory and bone before turning to fiction. They write from a small coastal town where they keep an unreasonable collection of antique lock-picks and insist none of them work.

chapters.title: Charms for the Forgetful
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the market city of Vell, Ada sells bone charms and hides the fact that she hears the dead whispering through them. A dying old woman buys a charm and begs Ada to 'remember Kestrelmark,' a name Ada has never heard. That night the stars go out and the border wards shatter like glass. Emotional beat: quiet dread breaking into wonder and fear.

chapters.title: The Country That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The city wakes with holes in its memory; streets lead nowhere, neighbors forget their own children. The dead grow loud, insisting Ada is a warden of Kestrelmark, a nation unmade five years ago. Ministry agents arrive hunting 'resonant objects' — her charms. Emotional beat: disorientation hardening into resolve as Ada realizes she cannot walk away.

chapters.title: A Thief with Good Timing
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, introducing Renn the smuggler. Renn breaks into Ada's workshop to steal her charms, then reveals he sold warden relics to the Ministry years ago — including, unknowingly, pieces of the Spire. Guilt-ridden, he offers passage out of the city. Ada refuses to flee; instead she demands he take her toward the Spire itself. Emotional beat: wary alliance forged from mutual shame.

chapters.title: The Ward-Singer's Silence
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren, a disgraced ward-singer who sang the wards that failed, lives drunk and anonymous in a river town. Ada finds her using the dead woman's charm as proof. Maren confesses she was ordered to sing the country closed and never learned why. She agrees to come — not for redemption, but because the silence in her head since the wards fell terrifies her more than guilt. Emotional beat: self-loathing meeting unexpected grace.

chapters.title: What the Dead Keep
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Traveling through erased villages, the group shelters in a chapel of bones where the dead show Ada Kestrelmark's final night: wardens sealing the Spire to hide it from the Ministry, at the cost of the country's existence. Ada learns the last dragon-fire, source of all waking magic, gutters beneath the Spire. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Apprentice at the Fireline
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, twelve, tends a dying flame in the mountains — the last vent of dragon-fire — believing her missing mother was a fire-keeper. Ministry hunters ambush the group; Maren sings a broken ward to save them and loses her voice for it. Tam joins them, carrying an ember in a lantern. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing around shared loss.

chapters.title: Ministry of Unmaking
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Captured and interrogated, Renn learns the Ministry didn't erase Kestrelmark by accident — its Director was a warden who chose oblivion after a catastrophe, and now wants the Spire dead forever so no one can undo her choice. Renn bargains their release by pretending to betray Ada, hating himself for how easily the lie comes. Emotional beat: betrayal as sacrifice, trust tested to cracking.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the Spire's threshold, the dragon-fire nearly dies; Tam's ember rekindles it, but the Spire demands a warden's true name to open. Ada understands the price: carving her name means being forgotten by everyone alive. Renn's false betrayal is exposed and forgiven; Maren writes her apology in ash since she cannot speak it. Emotional beat: terror and love arriving together.

chapters.title: Carve Me Out of the World
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax. Inside the waking Spire, Ada confronts the Director, who offers her a normal, remembered life if she walks away. Ada carves her name into the heartbone anyway; the stars reignite, Kestrelmark floods back into the world's memory, and the Director dissolves into the first starlight. Ada vanishes from every mind mid-embrace. Emotional beat: triumphant heartbreak — victory purchased with selfhood.

chapters.title: Remember Me Wrong, Remember Me Often
chapters.summary: Rotating POV — Maren, Renn, Tam. A year later, Kestrelmark thrives. The three refuse to let Ada stay forgotten: Maren regains her voice singing her story, Renn funds a shrine of charms, Tam keeps a flame lit 'for Ada, whoever she becomes.' A stranger with familiar hands arrives at the shrine, hearing the dead say one word: welcome. Emotional beat: belonging proven stronger than erasure; hope earned.
